topic.name: The Nth Term of an Arithmetic Sequence

question.text: Given an arithmetic sequence that has $a_{10}=23$ and the common difference $d=3$, what is the general formula for the $n$th term of the sequence?
question.explanation:
Since $a_{10}=23$ is $9$ jumps after $a_1,$ we can determine the first term of the sequence:

\begin{align*} a_{10} &= a_1 + 9d \\[3pt] 23 &= a_1 + 9(3) \\[3pt] 23 &= a_1 + 27 \\[3pt] -4 &= a_1 \end{align*}

So, the formula for the $n$th term is:

\begin{align*} a_{n} &= a_1 + (n-1)d \\[3pt] &= -4 + (n-1)(3) \\[3pt] &= -4 + 3n - 3 \\[3pt] &= 3n - 7 \end{align*}

example.title: Finding the Formula for the Nth Term Given Another Term and the Common Difference

question.text: Find the general formula for the $n$th term of the arithmetic sequence that begins with \[ 19, \: 17, \: 15, \: \ldots \]
question.explanation:
The formula for the $n$th term of an arithmetic sequence (in function notation) is

\[ f(n)= f(1)+(n-1)d. \]

From the first few terms

\[ 19, \: 17, \: 15, \: \ldots \]

we see that the first term is $f(1)=19$ and the common difference is \[ d= 17 - 19 = -2. \]

So, we substitute into the formula and simplify:

\begin{align} f(n) &= f(1)+(n-1)d\\[3pt] &= 19 + (n - 1)(-2) \\[3pt] &= 19 - 2n + 2\\[3pt] &= 21 - 2n \end{align}

Therefore, the formula for the $n$th term is $f(n) = 21 - 2n.$

example.title: Finding the Formula for the Nth Term of an Arithmetic Sequence in Function Notation

question.text: Find the $33$rd term of the following arithmetic sequence. \[ 13, \: 8, \: 3, \: -2, \: \ldots \]
question.explanation:
The formula for the $n$th term of an arithmetic sequence is

\[ a_n= a_{1}+(n-1)d. \]

First, we will write the formula for the $n$th term of this sequence. From the first few terms

\[ 13, \: 8, \: 3, \: -2, \: \ldots \]

we see that the first term is $a_1=13$ and the common difference is

\[ d=8-13=-5. \]

So, we substitute into the formula and simplify:

\[ \eqalign{ a_n&= a_{1}+(n-1)d\\[3pt] &= 13 + (n - 1)(-5) \\[3pt] & = 13 - 5n + 5 \\[3pt] &=18 - 5n } \]

Now, we can use our formula to find the $33$rd term. All we have to do is substitute $n=33\mathbin{:}$

\[ \eqalign{ a_n &=18 - 5n \\[3pt] a_{33} &= 18 - 5(33) \\[3pt] &= 18-165 \\[3pt] &= -147 } \]

Therefore, the $33$rd term of the sequence is $a_{33}=-147.$

example.title: Finding a Particular Term of an Arithmetic Sequence

question.text: Find the formula for the $n$th term of an arithmetic sequence if the first term is $-2$ and the second term is $3.$
question.explanation:
The formula for the $n$th term of an arithmetic sequence (in function notation) is

\[ f(n)= f(1)+(n-1)d. \]

We are given the first term $f(1)=-2.$ Also, the common difference of the sequence can be found as \[ d=3 - (-2) = 5. \]

So, we substitute into the formula and simplify: \begin{align*} f(n)&= f(1)+(n-1)d \\[5pt] &= -2 + (n - 1)(5) \\[5pt] &= -2 + 5n - 5 \\[5pt] &= \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{5n -7} \end{align*}

example.title: Finding the Formula for the Nth Term of an Arithmetic Sequence in Function Notation

question.text:
Consider the following arithmetic sequence.
\[
-17, \: -12, \: -7, \: -2, \: \ldots
\]
What is the $24$th term of this sequence?
question.explanation:
The formula for the $n$th term of an arithmetic sequence is \[ a_n= a_{1}+(n-1)d. \]

First, we will write the formula for the $n$th term of this sequence. From the first few terms \[ -17, \: -12, \: -7, \: -2, \: \ldots, \]

we see that the first term is $a_1=-17$ and the common difference is \[ d=-12-(-17)=5. \]

So, we substitute into the formula and simplify: \[ \eqalign{ a_n&= a_{1}+(n-1)d\\[5pt] &= -17 + (n - 1)(5) \\[5pt] & =-17 + 5n - 5 \\[5pt] &=5n - 22 } \]

Now, we can use our formula to find the $24$th term. All we have to do is substitute $n=24\mathbin{:}$ \[ \eqalign{ a_n &=5n-22 \\[5pt] a_{24} &= 5(24)-22 \\[5pt] &= 120-22 \\[5pt] &= \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{98} } \]
